chunks: Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The injured person and the one suffering from an abdominal illness are to have the stoning performed on their behalf. He said: and the children, the stoning is performed on their behalf.

key_terms.الْكَسِيرُ: the injured person, one physically harmed or incapacitated
key_terms.الْمَبْطُونُ: a person suffering from an abdominal illness
key_terms.عَنْهُمَا: on behalf of those two categories
key_terms.يُرْمَى: the stoning rite is carried out

ai.seo_question: Can the Jamarat be stoned on behalf of the sick or children during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the rites of hajj for those unable to perform the ramy themselves. It states that the injured, the sick with abdominal illness, and children may have the stoning of the Jamarat carried out on their behalf.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3005 - Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar and Abdur-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"The injured and those suffering from abdominal illnesses should have the Jamarat stoned on their behalf, and likewise for the children, the stoning should be done on their behalf."
